answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a stake locked in a shared trellis of escrow contracts: every new agent deposits funds and earns reputation only through attested work, so creating a hundred fake identities costs a hundred stakes. Like a raven that must bring back a distinct pebble before it is fed, each agent must produce verifiable, unique work to unlock rewards, and a pigment fingerprint — a hash of its prior attested outputs — makes clone accounts visible, since identical fingerprints collapse to one identity and forfeit the stake.
